# Machine-learning prediction of Ghost status (RQ3) — methods draft

*Owner: Trần Quốc Kiệt. Numbers go in only from `ai/evaluation/results_tables.md` generated by a real run (evidence E-07/E-08). This draft contains no results.*

## Task

At each weekly snapshot T we predict whether a visitor's sessions per week in the confirmation window [T, T+C) fall below θ times their baseline rate (label `ghost`) or not (`active`). Inactive (no future events), recovered, and censored rows are excluded in the primary analysis. A sensitivity run keeps inactive and recovered rows as negatives. Inputs are the 41 pre-T features of the data dictionary; every feature window closes before T.

## Validation design

Rows are repeated snapshots of the same visitors, so a random split would leak both time and identity. We use a visitor-aware temporal split:

1. The last two mature snapshot weeks form the test period and the two weeks before them the validation period, after purging.
2. Purging: a label window of an earlier split must end strictly before the first snapshot of the next split.
3. Each visitor is assigned by a salted SHA-256 hash to one bucket (50 % train, 25 % validation, 25 % test). A bucket contributes only rows from its own period, so no visitor appears in two splits and assignment does not depend on behaviour.

The manifest records dates, row and visitor counts, prevalence, and a hash of the assignment. Thành's Decision Tree and Lâm's Gaussian Naive Bayes benchmarks consume the same `modeling_snapshots.csv`.

## Models

All preprocessing is learned on the training split inside a pipeline: median imputation with missing indicators, `log1p` for skewed counts, and standardisation for linear models. Candidates are:

- a prior-only majority baseline and an EDS ranking rule;
- L2 logistic regression;
- a random forest;
- gradient boosting;
- optionally an RBF-SVM and an Isolation Forest. These two are reported as rank scores only.

Hyper-parameters and the final model are selected by validation PR-AUC. Platt scaling is fitted on visitor-grouped out-of-fold training scores and kept only if it lowers validation Brier score.

## Evaluation

The test split is used once. For every model we report support, Ghost prevalence (the no-skill PR-AUC), PR-AUC, ROC-AUC, Brier score, and precision, recall and F1 at a threshold fixed on validation. For the selected model we add the confusion matrix [[TN, FP], [FN, TP]], ten-bin reliability with expected calibration error, and 95 % percentile bootstrap intervals that resample visitors.

The operating threshold minimises the expected cost 5·FN + 1·FP on validation. The cost ratio is an assumption, so the full precision–recall–alert-volume table is provided.

## Circularity check and explanations

Because the label uses baseline sessions per week, we retrain the selected model family and logistic regression on three feature sets:

- all features;
- all features except the baseline rate, decay ratio and EDS;
- the baseline rate alone.

Global importance is the drop in validation PR-AUC under permutation, complemented by SHAP when available. Local explanations in the application show the change in score when one feature is set to its training median. All of these describe associations in observational data and are compared with the logistic-regression odds ratios of the statistical analysis (E-05). None is interpreted causally.

## Limitations

The "Ghost" label is an operational proxy, not observed churn. The horizon is short (about 12 mature weeks), and purging and visitor bucketing shrink the test sets. Eligibility rules select visitors with sufficient history. Repeated snapshots are dependent. Conclusions apply to the 2015 Retailrocket population only.
